article_title: GNU Coreutils 9.12 Ships With Faster cut, uniq, and sort Plus a New uname Labeling Option
summary: Manual editorial review overrides the automated APPROVE: all three quotes the article attributes to Phoronix as direct quotations are hallucinated (heavily paraphrased text presented inside quotation marks as if verbatim), including one in the article's lead paragraph.

findings.message: Hallucinated quote attributed to Phoronix in the article's lead paragraph (Overview section, sentence 2)
findings.details: Article states Phoronix wrote, verbatim in quotation marks: "GNU Coreutils 9.12 arrived today featuring bug fixes, fresh command options, and performance enhancements for this fundamental collection of system utilities." The actual sentence in the Phoronix snapshot (sources/2026-09/gnu-coreutils-912-ships-with-faster-cut-uniq-and-sort-plus-a-new-uname-labeling-option/source-0.html.gz) reads: "GNU Coreutils 9.12 released today with a mix of fixes, some new options, and various performance improvements to these widely-used set of core system utilities." No sentence matching the article's quoted wording appears anywhere in the snapshot. This is a fabricated quotation, not a verbatim reproduction, and it sits in the article's lead.

findings.message: Hallucinated quote attributed to Phoronix in the 'What We Know' section (recursive -R traversal paragraph)
findings.details: Article states, in quotation marks, that Phoronix "described the underlying problem as one where": "these utilities would encounter failures when using the recursive '-R' option if files were deleted concurrently during directory traversal operations." No such sentence appears in the Phoronix snapshot. The snapshot's actual wording is: "GNU Coreutils 9.12 addresses a long-standing bug where chcon, chgrp, chmod, chown, du, and ls would fail if traversing hierarchies with the recursive \"-R\" option and files were removed in parallel." Fabricated quotation, not verbatim.

findings.message: Hallucinated quote attributed to Phoronix in the 'What We Know' section (uname -A paragraph)
findings.details: Article states, in quotation marks, that Phoronix "described the new flags as displaying": "labeled output with individual items appearing on separate lines." No such sentence appears in the Phoronix snapshot. The snapshot's actual wording is: "The uname command also adds \"-A\" and \"--all-labeled\" options to label all output and showing one item per line." Fabricated quotation, not verbatim.

content_preview.title: GNU Coreutils 9.12 Ships With Faster cut, uniq, and sort Plus a New uname Labeling Option
content_preview.summary: GNU Coreutils 9.12 adds performance gains to cut, uniq, and sort, a new uname -A flag, and fixes for a factor buffer over-read and a parallel-deletion race.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

GNU Coreutils, the collection of core command-line utilities found on nearly every Linux and Unix-like system, has shipped version 9.12, according to the [project's official NEWS file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/coreutils/coreutils/master/NEWS), which dates the release "9.12 (2026-09-14) [stable]." [Phoronix](https://www.phoronix.com/news/GNU-Coreutils-9.12) reported the release the same day, writing that "GNU Coreutils 9.12 arrived today featuring bug fixes, fresh command op...

editor_notes.content_quality: The article is well-structured (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis), the technical explanations are clear, and the choice of a niche-but-widely-impactful release (coreutils touches essentially every Linux/Unix system) is a defensible News-category angle. Prose is neutral and free of sensationalism.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 3 snapshots in sources/2026-09/gnu-coreutils-912-ships-with-faster-cut-uniq-and-sort-plus-a-new-uname-labeling-option/ after re-hashing each decompressed file and confirming the sha256 matches manifest.json (source-0.html.gz, source-1.html.gz, source-2.html.gz all matched). source-1.html.gz (raw NEWS file from coreutils/coreutils master): checked all 17 direct quotes and specifics the article attributes to the NEWS file (release date '9.12 (2026-09-14) [stable]', the cut -w 4x throughput claim, uniq -c 2.5x claim, sort pipe-memory claim, the -R traversal race-condition fix wording, the factor CWE-126 buffer over-read and its 9.8 introduction, the cut -d multi-byte delimiter fix and its 9.11 introduction, the uname -A/--all-labeled wording, the cp/install/mv reflink fallback wording, the mv ENOTSUP xattr warning wording, the env/printenv QUOTING_STYLE wording, the env --env0-from=FILE wording, and the stat/tail failfs/nullfs wording) -- every one of these is a verbatim substring of the snapshot text. This source is quoted flawlessly. source-2.html.gz (GitHub release page for v9.12): confirmed the release was authored by GitHub user 'pixelb' (Pádraig Brady) on 14 Sep, and that the page states 'This tag was signed with the committer's verified signature. pixelb Pádraig Brady GPG key ID: DF6FD971306037D9 Verified' -- this fully supports the article's claim that 'The GitHub release tag for v9.12 is signed by maintainer Pádraig Brady.' source-0.html.gz (Phoronix article): the underlying facts the article paraphrases from Phoronix are all accurate (Phoronix did report the -R race fix, the uname -A option, the cut -w/uniq -c/sort improvements, the reflink fallback, and the mv xattr warning, on the same day as the NEWS release). However, all three passages the article places inside quotation marks and attributes to Phoronix as direct quotes ('GNU Coreutils 9.12 arrived today featuring...', 'these utilities would encounter failures when using the recursive...', and 'labeled output with individual items appearing on separate lines') are NOT verbatim text from the snapshot -- they are paraphrases of Phoronix's actual sentences, dressed up as exact quotations. I extracted the full plain text of the snapshot and grepped for the distinctive quoted phrases ('arrived today', 'fundamental collection', 'these utilities would encounter failures', 'labeled output with individual items appearing on separate lines'); none appear anywhere in the page. This is a hallucinated-quote pattern, not a single slip: 3 of 3 quotation-marked attributions to Phoronix in this article fail verbatim verification, and the first instance is in the article's lead paragraph (Overview, sentence 2).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specific technical claims (version numbers, performance multipliers, bug descriptions, CWE ID, introduced-in versions, flag names) are accurate and trace to the NEWS file or GitHub release page. No fabricated events, dates, or numbers. The sole accuracy problem is one of attribution/verbatim-quotation, not of underlying fact: the substance every fake Phoronix quote conveys is true and is independently confirmed elsewhere in the article via correctly-quoted NEWS text.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; no editorializing or sensational language.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for prior coreutils coverage. No existing article covers this specific 9.12 release; related prior pieces (Ubuntu 26.04's Rust coreutils, Microsoft's coreutils-for-Windows, apt's Rust rewrite) are about a different topic (Rust reimplementations of coreutils) and do not overlap with this GNU/upstream 9.12 release story. This is a genuinely new topic.
concerns: Three passages presented in quotation marks as direct quotes from Phoronix are not verbatim -- they are paraphrases of the source's actual wording, which is a hallucinated-quote pattern rather than an isolated slip.
One of the three fabricated quotes appears in the article's lead paragraph (Overview section), which per editorial policy pushes this past the threshold a single corrections note can honestly cover.

The pattern (100% of the article's Phoronix attributions fail verbatim verification, vs. 100% of its NEWS-file attributions passing) suggests a systemic issue in how this bot handled paraphrase-vs-quotation for the Phoronix source specifically, not a one-off typo.
recommendations: Resubmit as a new submission (not a rewrite of this one, per the v3.9.0 no-rewrite-cycle policy) with the three Phoronix attributions either converted to indirect/paraphrased attribution (no quotation marks) or replaced with the source's actual verbatim wording.
When quoting a source, copy the exact substring from the fetched snapshot rather than composing a paraphrase and wrapping it in quotation marks.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: REJECT. The underlying facts are accurate and well-sourced from the NEWS file (17/17 NEWS quotes verified verbatim) and the GitHub release page, and the article is otherwise well-written and neutral. But the article fabricates all three of its direct quotations attributed to Phoronix -- none of the quoted text is verbatim in the snapshot -- and one of those fabricated quotes is in the lead paragraph. Per review policy, a hallucinated quote in the headline/summary/lead is a REJECT trigger regardless of whether the paraphrased substance happens to be accurate, and a pattern of 3/3 failed verbatim-quote checks against the same source is not a single, isolated, correctable slip. A corrections note could restate the true Phoronix wording, but doing so for all three instances -- including the lead -- would amount to rewriting a third of the article's sourced quotations post-publication, which is not what the corrections mechanism is for.
